item.title: Nvidia's Huang Is a Gatekeeper on AI Regulation
item.description: Pick your favorite doomsday scenario for artificial intelligence. Whatever you choose, the road to prevention likely runs through Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: Why the Russia Election Actually Matters to Ukraine and Europe
item.description: In what must be the world’s least surprising election result, parties loyal to President Vladimir Putin have made a clean sweep in elections to Russia’s parliament, the State Duma. There’s little purpose to parsing who won what share of the vote; the point is that opponents of Putin and his war were either jailed, dead, in exile or banned from running. As a democratic exercise, this signified nothing — but it was an important moment nonetheless.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: France Is Living in Denial of Hard Economic Reality
item.description: A lengthy, two-part biopic of a mid-century politician would be an unlikely hit in most countries. But not, apparently, if the politician is Charles de Gaulle and the country is France. The films based on Julian Jackson’s 2018 biography of the general have seized the country’s imagination. They opened to a mere 380,000 viewers in their first days of screening, though — like de Gaulle himself — they grew in the telling. More than 5.5 million French people have seen them now.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Erdogan: The UN Must End the Security Council Veto
item.description: The tragedies of recent years, including pandemics, energy crises, disruptions to supply chains and regional conflicts, have demonstrated that leaving the resolution of global crises to the will of a handful of capitals is no longer compatible with the realities of today’s world. The adaptation of global decision-making mechanisms to today’s circumstances can no longer be postponed.
item.dc:creator: Recep Tayyip Erdogan

item.title: Oil Market: Iran War Supertankers Charge $1 Million a Day
item.description: Who’s winning the Iran war? The supertanker tycoons charging an arm and leg to cross Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Jollibee Shouldn’t Rush Its Global IPO
item.description: Jollibee Foods Corp. has spent two decades building a global restaurant empire. But while it makes sense for the Philippines’ fast-food powerhouse to separate the burgeoning international business from its mature, domestic operations, it shouldn’t rush to take the new company public.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.title: Lawsuit Over Trump’s Ban on CNN, MS NOW Is Ultimate Weapon
item.description: President Donald Trump surely knows by now that spontaneously banning media from the White House is illegal. He even has alternative — and legitimate — methods to revoke credentials that wouldn’t be so toxic to free speech.
item.dc:creator: Barbara McQuade

item.title: Passive Retirement Investing Raises Systemic Risk for US Markets
item.description: Like it or not, we are all betting on AI taking over the economy. In the last 40 years, the US has become a nation of stock investors. On the whole, it has made Americans rich. Now the stock market is soaring on the hopes that AI will make everyone more productive — and if that doesn’t work out, we all may learn the definition of a bad tail risk.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: A Texas Magnet Plant Shows US Manufacturing Can Return — at a Cost
item.description: On former farmland on the outskirts of Fort Worth, Texas, a brand-new 250,000-square-foot factory stands as a symbol that the US can return to its roots of making things.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Can Democrats' Blue-Collar Brigade Win Working-Class Voters?
item.description: Sam Forstag recently joined a text chain to better keep up with a few friends. There’s nothing unusual about that, except Forstag’s texting buddies are a group of Democratic candidates for the US House who share one unusual characteristic: They have spent years in blue-collar jobs.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein

item.title: Midterms: Democrats Are Set to Win the House but Not in a Blue Wave
item.description: The Republican majority in the House of Representatives is almost certainly headed for a massive whupping in the upcoming midterm elections. But the tussle for the speaker’s gavel is not unfolding, and may not finish, like the thumpings and shellackings of yesteryear.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: Pete Hegseth's Pentagon Purges Must Be Stopped by Congress
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his critics agree on one thing: The Pentagon is in urgent need of transformation. The change he’s pursuing, however, is endangering that vital mission.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Crypto Can't Go Mainstream Without the Clarity Act
item.description: US regulators are determined to boost cryptoassets. That’s unsurprising when they owe their jobs to the meme-coin billionaire (and US President) Donald Trump. But after the Senate last week voted down the wide-ranging Clarity Act, any efforts by market watchdogs to codify rules for digital-asset markets risk being shot down by the next administration. And worse, the Supreme Court has already undercut agency rulemaking powers, anyway.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit: China’s Leverage Makes It Key to Any Iran War Deal
item.description: At the BRICS summit in New Delhi on Sept. 12, 2026, Xi Jinping called for a more active role for China and other member countries in ending the war with Iran. China’s president said the conflict had inflicted serious losses across the region, was against the common interests of the international community, and should give way to a “permanent, comprehensive ceasefire” and a new regional security architecture. China, he added, would work with other BRICS members to play its “due role” in bringing
item.dc:creator: Simon Johnson and Amir Kermani

item.title: Germany Is Stuck With Merz When It Needs a Klopp
item.description: Two more humiliating regional election results in eastern Germany have dealt conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s authority a heavy blow. Rather than fall on his sword, Germany’s unpopular leader is urging patience while reforms continue.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bryant
